observation: Genomic assembly fidelity requires actual read-window support and quality decisions, not a copied expected contig file. This study checks every occupied k-mer count/quality/extension/actual-hash record, visited-key set, and full walk/temp buffer against an independent read Counter and de Bruijn graph oracle. Five cases cover supported extension, equal-support fork, low-quality rejection, low-only support, and a repeat cycle. The native broadcast fix is a separate conditional stratum: source initialization is defective even though its minimal GPU probe happened to produce expected values. All Julia versions use a CUDA-specific NVVM cohort intrinsic, so none is advertised as a pure backend-neutral mapping. AoS-to-SoA layout and register policies limit framework-only performance attribution. Left reverse-complement/stitching and full biological datasets remain explicitly unmeasured.
effort_observation: Shared reference work includes two successful feature probes (original/fixed broadcast, exact NVVM match-any), one auxiliary Python fixture parse repair and one strict reuse-contract guard rejection. CUDA.jl had two observed runtime repairs across three full candidate/check processes: shuffle API indexing, then register resources. KA passed one candidate/check on its public static-workgroup launch path. JACC had one observed register-resource runtime failure and passed candidate/check 2 using an explicitly pinned compiler-control adapter, not a replacement device kernel. Native conditional full pipeline passed its first candidate/check.
